title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed, numbered sheet ('- 42 -', 'n° 382') from what looks like a Bourbaki rédaction. The terminology ('subimmersion', manifolds over a complete valued field K, numbered paragraphs 4.12.x) points to a draft of Bourbaki's 'Variétés différentielles et analytiques. Fascicule de résultats'. The surrounding pages are handwritten notes on the Hodge–Tate decomposition for CM abelian varieties. Grothendieck evidently used the back of this sheet as scrap paper, and it was scanned in sequence.

The typed mathematics:
(1) Definition of a left action of a Lie group G on a manifold X: s(tx) = (st)x and ex = x.
(2) Orbit and stabilizer. Suppose the orbit map g ↦ g·x is a subimmersion, i.e. locally of constant rank. This holds automatically when char K = 0. Then:
- the stabilizer G_x is a Lie subgroup;
- the induced map G/G_x → X is an immersion.
If moreover the orbit Gx is locally closed and G has a countable base, then Gx is a submanifold and G/G_x → Gx is an isomorphism. This is a Baire-category argument.
(3) 4.12.6 defines an S-group, i.e. a family of Lie groups parametrised by S. Let π: G → S be a submersion whose fibres G_s carry group structures such that:
- the unit section e: S → G is a morphism;
- (x,y) ↦ x⁻¹y on G ×_S G is a morphism.
It follows that the fibres are Lie groups, inversion is a morphism, and multiplication is a morphism.
(4) 4.12.7 introduces the 'functor of points'. For f: T → S, G(T) is the set of sections over f, i.e. morphisms φ: T → G with π∘φ = f. It is a group under pointwise multiplication via G ×_S G, with neutral element e∘f.

All of this is standard foundational material on Lie groups and families of Lie groups over a valued field, written in Bourbaki's style.
errors: In 4.12.6 (i), 's ∈ G' should read 's ∈ S'. This is a typing slip in the original.

No mathematical errors otherwise. The claim that the subimmersion hypothesis is automatic in characteristic 0 is correct: the orbit map has constant rank by homogeneity. In characteristic p it can fail.

ideas.what: Orbit–stabilizer theorem for Lie group actions over a complete valued field: G/G_x → X is an immersion under a subimmersion hypothesis, and an isomorphism onto a locally closed orbit if G is second countable.
ideas.modern_name: Homogeneous spaces / orbit theorem for Lie groups over K
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lie, Cartan, Chevalley); in this generality Bourbaki and Serre (Lie Algebras and Lie Groups)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Variétés différentielles et analytiques, Fascicule de résultats; Bourbaki Lie III

ideas.what: Definition of an S-group: a submersion with fibrewise group laws such that the unit section and (x,y) ↦ x⁻¹y are morphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Family of Lie groups / group object over S in the category of manifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bourbaki; analogous to group schemes over S (Grothendieck, SGA 3)
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki VAR R (fascicule de résultats); the scheme analogue is in SGA 3 Exp. I

ideas.what: The group of sections G(T) for a base change T → S.
ideas.modern_name: Functor of points of a relative group object
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (functorial viewpoint, FGA/SGA 3), adopted here by Bourbaki

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed Bourbaki draft sheet reused as scratch paper, not Grothendieck's own work. Its content is standard published foundational material on Lie group actions and families of Lie groups. The real mathematics of this folder at this point (the Hodge–Tate decomposition for CM abelian varieties) is on the neighbouring handwritten pages, not here.
transcription_corrections: In 4.12.6 (i) the image indeed reads 's ∈ G'. This is a typo in the original for 's ∈ S'; the transcription is faithful.
The header 'n° 382' is a Bourbaki rédaction number, not a Grothendieck page number. The handwritten '54' at the bottom left is the archive page number.
